correctness.rationale: Strict Euclidean norm convexity makes all maximizers diametral vertex pairs; supporting gradients make cone slices compact; the exact squared-distance inequality gives a uniformly controlled radial boundary and O(epsilon^{2d+2}) absolute remainder; coarea, beta and Dirichlet integrations determine the constants and conditional laws. Box coefficients follow by direct linear ray coordinates and Dirichlet moments. Finite numerical checks additionally agree, but are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The all-dimensional two-term Euclidean distance tail and conditional limiting endpoint geometry are neither the previously published marginal polygon distance formulas nor n-sample symmetric extreme-value laws. The conditional cone-mixture and Dirichlet shape theorem are additional assertions that a marginal distance distribution cannot by itself determine. Plausible primary full texts not wholly accessible remain acknowledged risks; no exhaustive uniqueness is claimed.
residual_risks: The complete 2016 arbitrary-polygon PDD article could imply the dimension-two scalar coefficient even without naming it.
The 2002 sample-diameter article and more general local polyhedral extreme-value literature were not examined in full; a general result may subsume part of the theorem.
Published-record search coverage is bounded and is not proof of global originality.

value.rationale: The natural fixed-two extreme Euclidean distance event probes all diameter-supporting cone pairs. The positive transverse second coefficient is structural rather than a gratuitous extra term, and the conditional Dirichlet shape law reveals endpoint geometry absent from marginal statistics. Sharp box fixed-volume minimization supplies a meaningful consequence and check; validity is not inferred from computational verification alone.
